learn.title: Why not an array?
learn.body: An array needs one block of memory and a size chosen early. A linked list instead builds a chain of small pieces called nodes, each created when needed with `malloc`. Each node knows where the next one is.

learn.title: A node
learn.body: A node holds a value and a pointer to the next node. The name `struct node` is needed inside, because `node` is not defined yet.

learn.title: NULL ends the chain
learn.body: The last node's `next` is NULL, which means there is nothing after it. The program keeps one pointer, often called `head`, to the first node. Lose it and you lose the whole list.

learn.title: Making one node
learn.body: `n->value` is shorthand for `(*n).value`. Setting next to NULL matters: malloc leaves it with garbage.

learn.title: Reading a chain
learn.body: Head points to node A (value 4). A's next points to B (value 9). B's next is NULL.
steps: `head->next->next` is NULL, so the list has two nodes

questions.prompt: What does a node's `next` pointer hold?
choices: The address of the following node
The value of the next node
A copy of the next node
questions.explanation: The pointer lets you reach the next node wherever malloc placed it.

questions.prompt: What marks the end of a list?
choices: A node whose next is NULL

questions.prompt: To reach the value of a node through pointer `n`, write n\_\_value.
questions.explanation: `->` follows the pointer and then picks the field.

questions.prompt: Why is `struct node *next` used inside the struct?
choices: The typedef name does not exist yet there
questions.explanation: The name `node` is only created after the closing brace, so the struct needs its own full name.

questions.prompt: A node is created with malloc and `next` was never set. What should you set it to? (one word)
questions.explanation: malloc does not clear memory, so set next to NULL to avoid a garbage pointer.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to create one node.
steps: Check the result is not NULL
Use the node and later free it
questions.explanation: Never use the memory before checking the allocation worked.
